claims.claim_text: Dietary fiber consists of nondigestible carbohydrates and lignin that are intrinsic and intact in plants.
claims.evidence_statement: Dietary fiber is defined by consensus bodies and review literature as plant material resistant to human digestive enzymes.
claims.interpretation: Helps learners distinguish fiber from digestible carbohydrates.
claims.practical_advice: Emphasize whole-plant foods (vegetables, fruits, legumes, whole grains) as sources of intact fiber.
claims.limitations: Definitions can vary slightly by regulatory body.

claims.claim_text: Higher dietary fiber intake is associated with greater microbial diversity and increased short-chain fatty acid production.
claims.evidence_statement: Observational and intervention studies report associations between higher fiber intake, gut microbial diversity, and fermentation metabolites such as butyrate.
claims.interpretation: Fiber provides substrates for microbial fermentation, but individual responses vary.
claims.practical_advice: Include a variety of fiber-rich plant foods to support microbial diversity rather than relying on a single source.
claims.limitations: Observational associations; microbiota measures are biomarkers, not clinical outcomes; inter-individual variability is large.

claims.claim_text: Higher fiber intake is associated with lower risk of cardiovascular disease and all-cause mortality in prospective cohorts.
claims.evidence_statement: Meta-analyses of prospective cohort studies report inverse associations between higher fiber intake and cardiovascular disease incidence and all-cause mortality.
claims.interpretation: Higher fiber intake correlates with better health outcomes, but this does not prove fiber alone prevents disease.
claims.practical_advice: Recommend fiber-rich dietary patterns consistent with dietary guidelines, not isolated supplements for disease prevention.
claims.study_design: Systematic review and meta-analysis of prospective cohorts
claims.limitations: Observational data with residual confounding; fiber intake correlated with other healthy behaviors.

claims.claim_text: Many adults do not meet recommended fiber intake levels.
claims.evidence_statement: Population surveys and dietary guidelines report that average fiber intake is below recommended levels for many adults.
claims.interpretation: A practical gap exists between recommendations and typical intake.
claims.practical_advice: Help learners identify small swaps (e.g., whole grain for refined grain, legumes, vegetables) to gradually increase fiber intake.
claims.limitations: Intake estimates depend on self-reported dietary data.

claims.claim_text: Choosing fiber-rich whole plant foods can help adults move toward recommended dietary patterns.
claims.evidence_statement: Dietary guidance emphasizes vegetables, fruits, whole grains, legumes, nuts, and seeds as food sources of dietary fiber.
claims.interpretation: A practical, food-based strategy for increasing fiber intake.
claims.practical_advice: Use small food substitutions, such as whole grains for refined grains, and add legumes, vegetables, fruits, nuts, or seeds; individual needs and tolerance vary.
claims.limitations: Population-level guidance; individual medical conditions may require tailored advice.
